newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim meets opposition over labour law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim meets opposition over labour law.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam met opposition leaders on Tuesday to try to reach compromise over a new labour law that triggered more than three weeks of wildcat srikes, a presidential spokesman said.
He said the meeting began around midday (0300 GMT).
The spokesman said no time limit was set for the talks at the presidential Blue House. Yonhap Television News said the lunch meeting would last about two hours.

Kim was holding discussions with Kim Dae-jung of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics and Kim Jong-pil of the United Liberal Democratic Party, the spokesman said. Lee Hong-koo of the ruling New Korea Party was also present.
Attention has been riveted on the meeting since Kim, in a dramatic turnaround, agreed to discuss opposition criticism of the legislation that makes it easier for firms to lay off workers.
On Monday unionists returned to work after the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions called off indefinite strikes.
